     3	ufo2ft
     4	======
     5	
     6	ufo2ft ("UFO to FontTools") is a fork of
     7	`ufo2fdk <https://github.com/typesupply/ufo2fdk>`__ whose goal is to
     8	generate OpenType font binaries from UFOs without the FDK dependency.
     9	
    10	The library provides two functions, ``compileOTF`` and ``compileTTF``,
    11	which work exactly the same way:
    12	
    13	.. code:: python
    14	
    15	    from defcon import Font
    16	    from ufo2ft import compileOTF
    17	    ufo = Font('MyFont-Regular.ufo')
    18	    otf = compileOTF(ufo)
    19	    otf.save('MyFont-Regular.otf')
    20	
    21	In most cases, the behavior of ufo2ft should match that of ufo2fdk,
    22	whose documentation is retained below (and hopefully is still accurate).
    23	
    24	Naming Data
    25	~~~~~~~~~~~
    26	
    27	As with any OpenType compiler, you have to set the font naming data to a
    28	particular standard for your naming to be set correctly. In ufo2fdk, you
    29	can get away with setting *two* naming attributes in your font.info
    30	object for simple fonts:
    31	
    32	-  familyName: The name for your family. For example, "My Garamond".
    33	-  styleName: The style name for this particular font. For example,
    34	   "Display Light Italic"
    35	
    36	ufo2fdk will create all of the other naming data based on thse two
    37	fields. If you want to use the fully automatic naming system, all of the
    38	other name attributes should be set to ``None`` in your font. However,
    39	if you want to override the automated system at any level, you can
    40	specify particular naming attributes and ufo2fdk will honor your
    41	settings. You don't have to set *all* of the attributes, just the ones
    42	you don't want to be automated. For example, in the family "My Garamond"
    43	you have eight weights. It would be nice to style map the italics to the
    44	romans for each weight. To do this, in the individual romans and
    45	italics, you need to set the style mapping data. This is done through
    46	the ``styleMapFamilyName`` and ``styleMapStyleName`` attributes. In each
    47	of your roman and italic pairs you would do this:
    48	
    49	**My Garamond-Light.ufo**
    50	
    51	-  familyName = "My Garamond"
    52	-  styleName = "Light"
    53	-  styleMapFamilyName = "My Garamond Display Light"
    54	-  styleMapStyleName = "regular"
    55	
    56	**My Garamond-Light Italic.ufo**
    57	
    58	-  familyName = "My Garamond"
    59	-  styleName = "Display Light Italic"
    60	-  styleMapFamilyName = "My Garamond Display Light"
    61	-  styleMapStyleName = "italic"
    62	
    63	**My Garamond-Book.ufo**
    64	
    65	-  familyName = "My Garamond"
    66	-  styleName = "Book"
    67	-  styleMapFamilyName = "My Garamond Display Book"
    68	-  styleMapStyleName = "regular"
    69	
    70	**My Garamond-Book Italic.ufo**
    71	
    72	-  familyName = "My Garamond"
    73	-  styleName = "Display Book Italic"
    74	-  styleMapFamilyName = "My Garamond Display Book"
    75	-  styleMapStyleName = "italic"
    76	
    77	**etc.**
    78	
    79	Additionally, if you have defined any naming data, or any data for that
    80	matter, in table definitions within your font's features that data will
    81	be honored.
    82	
    83	
    84	Feature generation
    85	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    86	
    87	If your font's features do not contain kerning/mark/mkmk features,
    88	ufo2ft will create them based on your font's kerning/anchor data.
    89	
    90	In addition to
    91	`Adobe OpenType feature files <http://www.adobe.com/devnet/opentype/afdko/topic_feature_file_syntax.html>`__,
    92	ufo2ft also supports the
    93	`MTI/Monotype format <http://monotype.github.io/OpenType_Table_Source/otl_source.html>`__.
    94	For example, a GPOS table in this format would be stored within the UFO at
    95	``data/com.github.googlei18n.ufo2ft.mtiFeatures/GPOS.mti``.
    96	
    97	
    98	Fallbacks
    99	~~~~~~~~~
   100	
   101	Most of the fallbacks have static values. To see what is set for these,
   102	look at ``fontInfoData.py`` in the source code.
   103	
   104	In some cases, the fallback values are dynamically generated from other
   105	data in the info object. These are handled internally with functions.
   106	
   107	Merging TTX
   108	~~~~~~~~~~~
   109	
   110	If the UFO data directory has a ``com.github.fonttools.ttx`` folder with TTX
   111	files ending with ``.ttx``, these will be merged in the generated font.
   112	The index TTX (generated when using using ``ttx -s``) is not required.

   124	Color fonts
   125	~~~~~~~~~~~
   126	
   127	ufo2ft supports building ``COLR`` and ``CPAL`` tables.
   128	
   129	If there is ``com.github.googlei18n.ufo2ft.colorPalettes`` key in font lib, and
   130	``com.github.googlei18n.ufo2ft.colorLayerMapping`` key in the font or
   131	in any of the glyphs lib, then ufo2ft will build ``CPAL`` table from the color
   132	palettes, and ``COLR`` table from the color layers.
   133	
   134	``colorPalettes`` is a array of palettes, each palette is a array of colors and
   135	each color is a array of floats representing RGBA colors. For example:
   136	
   137	.. code:: xml
   138	
   139	    <key>com.github.googlei18n.ufo2ft.colorPalettes</key>
   140	    <array>
   141	      <array>
   142	        <array>
   143	          <real>0.26</real>
   144	          <real>0.0</real>
   145	          <real>0.23</real>
   146	          <real>1.0</real>
   147	        </array>
   148	        <array>
   149	          <real>0.86</real>
   150	          <real>0.73</real>
   151	          <real>0.28</real>
   152	          <real>1.0</real>
   153	        </array>
   154	      </array>
   155	    </array>
   156	
   157	
   158	``colorLayerMapping`` is a array of color layers, each color layer is a array of

   161	
   162	.. code:: xml
   163	
   164	      <key>com.github.googlei18n.ufo2ft.colorLayerMapping</key>
   165	      <array>
   166	        <array>
   167	          <string>color.1</string>
   168	          <integer>1</integer>
   169	        </array>
   170	        <array>
   171	          <string>color.2</string>
   172	          <integer>0</integer>
   173	        </array>
   174	      </array>
   175	
   176	With these this key present, ufo2ft will copy the color layers into individual
   177	glyphs and setup ``COLR`` table.
